input.task: Add visible keyboard-focus indicators to the landing page

acceptanceCriteria.claim: After tabbing through the page with the keyboard (no mouse), the currently focused nav element shows a clearly visible violet focus ring around it
acceptanceCriteria.navigationHint: open the landing page root and press Tab seven times to move keyboard focus to the 'Get started' button in the nav

input.plan: Add a single `.lp a:focus-visible, .lp button:focus-visible` rule (violet outline, offset, rounded) so links/buttons get a clear on-brand focus indicator. The landing page previously had zero focus-visible styling of its own — keyboard users fell back to whatever the browser's default (if any) rendered.
decisions: Used :focus-visible rather than :focus so mouse clicks don't show the ring, only actual keyboard navigation does — avoids the classic 'ugly outline on every click' complaint while keeping it for keyboard users

Scoped the rule to `.lp a, .lp button` (matches every interactive element already on the page) instead of per-component rules, since the page has no custom-styled form controls needing different treatment
rejectedAlternatives: Per-button focus styles (e.g. only .btn:focus-visible) — rejected because the six plain nav/footer links needed the same treatment and a single shared rule covers both with less duplication

promptLog.text: Yes [open one more small PR with an actual visual change so I can see the GIF + screenshots embedded inline for real]

Adding visible keyboard-focus indicators to the landing page — a genuine, small accessibility gap (no :focus-visible styling existed at all) — and running receipts qa/build against it so this PR's CI run exercises the real visual-claim path end to end.
